newsitem.title: USA: Status of 14 Cubans in Florida uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Status of 14 Cubans in Florida uncertain.

text.p: Fourteen Cubans who sailed across to Florida awaited word on their future on Monday in what could be the first test for proposed changes to U.S. policy on illegal immigrants from the Communist-ruled island.

A spokesman for the U.S. Immigration & Naturalisation Service said they arrived in the Florida Keys near Key Largo by boat on Sunday after spending four or five days at sea. The group included 10 adult men, two women, a 17-year-old boy and a 6-year-old girl.

The minors were released to local community agencies, their parents were being held at the Krome Immigrant Processing Centre outside Miami and the rest of the group were in detention near Sarasota, Florida.

For three decades, virtually all Cubans arriving in the United States have been allowed to stay, regardless of whether they arrived legally or illegally, reflecting U.S. opposition to the government of Cuban President Fidel Castro.

In May 1995, Washington agreed to send back to Cuba illegal migrants who were intercepted at sea while trying to reach the United States. But the relatively few Cubans who reached the U.S. mainland still were allowed to remain.

U.S. and Cuban officials said this month they had agreed to work toward an accord under which the United States would repatriate Cubans arriving illegally. But the INS spokesman in Miami said he had no indication of any policy shift that would change the way Sunday's arrivals would be treated. "It's business as usual," he said.
The U.S. Coast Guard, meanwhile, said it repatriated five Cuban migrants on Monday at Bahia de Cabanas, Cuba.

The migrants were among seven Cubans -- five men, a woman and a girl -- who were rescued on Friday from a 22-foot (7-meter) boat that was disabled and adrift near Key West, Florida. INS agents determined that two of the men should be taken to the United States.
